recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is for core. If the work group wants the historical informational diagnostic strengthened into a build-failing error, that follow-up belongs in Kindling tooling source/release rather than in current FHIR specification source files.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive STU3 FHIR-Tools-Core request to report an error when a resource spreadsheet contains an unrecognized mapping column, using Condition's "Workflow Mappings" heading as the example of a typo for valid "Workflow Mapping".
initial_application: Jira's implementation comment points to svn revision 12607, mirrored as git commit a444eaf408607d2f8eb0f04508bf5f1675aaf0fa. That commit added ignored-mapping-column detection to the old spreadsheet parser, stored the messages as ResourceDefn hints, and emitted them through ResourceValidator as informational hints; it also added spreadsheet comments telling editors to use column names from source/mappingSpaces.xml.
additional_context: The current checkout no longer carries the old parser Java source directly. build.gradle.kts depends on org.hl7.fhir:kindling and gradle.properties pins kindlingVersion to 1.25.5-SNAPSHOT. Decompiling the cached Kindling jar shows OldSpreadsheetParser.checkIgnoredColumns still compares mapping-column headings with MappingSpace column names and ResourceValidator still emits ResourceDefn hints. source/mappingSpaces.xml defines the valid Workflow Mapping heading, source/fhir.ini keeps Condition and workflow extension sources in build scope, and rg found no current Workflow Mappings heading in source spreadsheets.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No FHIR-core source file was changed because the historical tooling behavior remains present through the current Kindling dependency and current checked-in source does not contain the cited bad column heading.
